That keeps things readable. Looking at that first card, the very long title is trimmed to a few lines with a little "…", the description is capped the same way, and instead of a messy row of every label it shows three and then "+4 more." So even a link with a mouthful of a title and a pile of labels sits in a tidy card the same size as the others — my eye can still skim down the list without one overstuffed item throwing everything off. That's the readability-first look I wanted from the start.

And the tradeoff feels right. The card is just the glance — enough to recognize it — so trimming it is fine as long as nothing's actually lost. Keeping the full title, the whole description, and every label available when I open the details means I can always get the complete picture when I want it. So nothing's hidden, just neatly folded away. Good balance.
